channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Perspective: Engage with diverse art to combat shrinking inclusive efforts
item.description: As President Donald Trump-era policies targeting diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives prompt GW to remove their DEI pages, rename diversity-focused events and halt hiring for positions related to diversity, it's crucial that the student body makes a concerted effort to engage with diverse perspectives. Creative media can play an influential role in this.

item.title: Hard bargaining slows GW Hospital nurses’ contract talks, union leader says
item.description: One year after bargaining began, the GW Hospital nurses union are still negotiating their first contract, citing “hard bargaining” and GW Hospital management limits to bargaining sessions as the reasons for the delay.

item.title: Op-ed: Students see the problems at GW. It’s time to step up and lead
item.description: This spring, the student body will choose new SGA leadership through an open election, and all students can throw their hat in the ring.

item.title: Men’s basketball manager squad reaches national rankings
item.description: For the first time in program history, the men’s basketball Manager Games team has cracked national rankings landing at No. 21 in the Manager Games Top 25 — the only Atlantic 10 team to reach that feat.

item.title: Crime log: GWPD receives report of student urinating in flower bed
item.description: Liquor Law Violation Clark Hall 2/24/2026 – 10:46 p.m. Closed Case The GW Police Department and an administrator on-call responded to a report of non-GW-affiliated individuals in the basement. The administrator on-call observed an alcoholic beverage in plain view and disposed of the alcohol on-scene. – Case closed. Referred to Conflict Education & Student Accountability....

item.title: Pentagon terminates GW fellowship over alleged anti-military bias
item.description: A memo signed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirms the Pentagon will bar senior military officers from studying in fellowships with the University starting next academic year due to the GW's alleged “anti-American resentment and military disdain."

item.title: Faculty senators ask officials to make clearer use of executive sessions during meetings
item.description: Faculty senators said officials’ executive sessions during their public meetings lack justification for privacy, limiting transparency because the discussions don’t involve information that the senate needs to keep confidential from the rest of the community.

item.title: US-Israeli strikes on Iran trigger protest, celebration across District
item.description: Demonstrations both celebrating and condemning the U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran cropped up around the District on Saturday.

item.title: Bass departs SMHS, leaving behind a complicated legacy
item.description: Retiring School of Medicine & Health Sciences Dean Barbara Bass concluded her tenure marked by a consequential leadership legacy on Saturday.

item.title: GW sold Virginia campus for $427 million to Amazon for data center development
item.description: The deal transfers all of GW’s roughly 122 acres of property in Loudoun County, Virginia, to ADS for $427,299,350 — roughly $3.5 million an acre — according to real estate records.
